newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dongfang 1996 net profit falls five pct.
newsitem.headline: Dongfang 1996 net profit falls five pct.

text.p: Guangzhou Dongfang Hotel Co Ltd said on Thursday its net profits slipped 4.99 percent in 1996 from the previous year due to increased competition.
The five-star hotelier said in an annual report published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times that after-tax profit was 53.86 million yuan last year versus 56.69 million yuan in 1995.
Earnings per share were 0.33 yuan against 0.38 yuan in 1995 and main operating income dropped 23.87 percent to 195.28 million yuan from 256.50 million yuan, Dongfang said.
The company said the lower profits were mainly due to fiercer competition, which forced it to cut room rates by an average of 17 percent in 1996.

Dongfang said it plans to issue a dividend of 2.00 yuan per share and distribute one bonus share for every 10 shares held. The proposal requires approval from shareholders who will meet in the near future, it said without further detail.
The firm said earlier it planned a 2.7-for-10 rights offer, tentatively priced at three to five yuan per rights share, based on share capital of 163.34 million shares at the end of 1996.
It aims to complete the plan by April 30 pending final approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Proceeds would be used to expand operations via acquisitions.
